name: London Hall
summary: Buff-brick wings frame a lawn behind a two-storey glass lobby, with the east wing rising above the entrance canopy. The lower Western Road wing has evenly spaced bedroom windows and vertical stacks of blue-grey panels.

evidence.note: U-shaped plan open to the south, with a low roof across the north entrance, a long west wing and shorter, taller east wing. Long service strips appear on both main roofs. Gravel sampled at local (75,1243).

Regional 2 m grid, heights above local ground. Median 14.61 m, P90 21.4 m, maximum 27.35 m. Western roof mostly 14–15 m, east roof 20–21 m, north lobby 7–9 m. A raised core near (112,1217) reaches 27 m.
Western Road facade has four rows of windows, long paired window groupings and blue-grey sheet spandrels alternating with warm brick.
Oblique corner shows extensive brick with vertically aligned metal-framed windows.
Tall recessed glass doors, a two-storey glazed lobby and a projecting roof slab with a warm soffit in front of the high eastern core.
Frontal view locates double doors under the canopy return. Masonry piers separate the two-storey panes.
Western street approach continues the pale bedroom bays towards the southern end.
PIL mean from brick at normalized (0.20,0.60) and pale spandrel at (0.079,0.15). Full elevation shows vent lights, aluminum mullions and contrasting spandrel panels.
Garden-side connector has three great vertical bays, tall glazed ground openings and smaller bedroom windows above.
Architect confirms the double-height entrance lobby and meeting spaces.

Comparing 138541239 and 130394509 places the recessed paired door at the west end of wall 20 under the main high roof. The cantilever is continuous with the two-storey lobby roof. The raised eastern core has windows on its upper storeys. Frame 66665193 shows repeated vertical stacks of blue-grey panels.

notes: Bedroom-bay counts on the far east and south returns are estimates. Stack blue-grey spandrels only in selected bays. Exposed wood linings follow the broad offset entrance roof. The 1 m lidar grid resolves stepped core roofs at 24.4 and 27.1 m, a lobby roof near 10 m and a 3–4 m extension at the southern end of the east wing. North lobby glass ends at the lower roof. The sheltered timber underside has a separate pale metal top edge; the Western Road bedrooms above use brick and grouped sashes.
